body: Claim (family member): dispatched together with #13028 on branch `claude/issue-13028-composition-seam-family` — see the chain-lead claim there for the full serial-constraint and family-gate record. Session: `session_71836b57-5db6-459d-ae4d-c6d9d7dd2cc6`.

Family member — implemented on branch `claude/issue-13028-composition-seam-family` together with #13028. Draft PR: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/13057

The `os-dev-report` for this family lives on the chain-lead card: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/13028#issuecomment-5459500792

This member in one line: `os migrate plan` / `apply` now end the process deliberately once their document is written, after the kernel teardown they already ran, draining stdout and stderr first (a `--json` payload on a pipe must not truncate) under a bounded wait. Regression pin is `packages/cli/test/migrate-plan-exits.e2e.test.ts`, which spawns a real child against a fixture whose host plugin arms a ref'd interval in `init()` and would clear it in the suppressed `start()`: 2s and exit 0 with the fix, and — ablated, disk-proven — killed at 90053ms without it.

⚠️ One verified consumer-side finding this PR does NOT fix, recorded for the PM: ObjectStack Cloud's `lazyPlugin` wrapper (`packages/service-cloud/src/control-plane-preset.ts`) defines `init`/`start`/`stop` and no `destroy`, while the kernel's only teardown entry point is `plugin.destroy()` — nothing in `packages/core/src` ever calls `plugin.stop()`. So roughly twenty control-plane plugins release nothing on shutdown in every cloud boot, `os serve` included. That is the cloud-side root of this card; the framework half landed here makes the command exit regardless of what the host left running.
